`person:group-hinduja` · flag: **mixed** · confidence: verified · tickers: INDUSINDBK, ASHOKLEY, HGS, GULFOILLUB, RELCAPITAL

Flag: MIXED. London/Geneva-based family controlling Ashok Leyland, Gulf Oil Lubricants, Hinduja Global Solutions (HGS) and, through IndusInd International Holdings (IIHL, Mauritius), IndusInd Bank; IIHL also won Reliance Capital in IBC (Rs 9,650 cr plan, 2024-25). Family: a 2014 letter said assets in any brother's name belonged to all four; Srichand Hinduja's side sued (UK High Court, 2020) to declare it void; a truce was announced (2022); Srichand died May-2023 and chairman Gopichand died 4-Nov-2025, with succession reports conflicting (Prakash/Ashok vs. third-generation Dheeraj/Sanjay). A Geneva court (Jun-2024) convicted four family members of exploiting domestic staff (acquitted of trafficking) -- personal, not listed-company, conduct. Listed-company issues: IndusInd Bank's derivatives-accounting discrepancy (~Rs 1,960 cr, disclosed Mar-2025), plus ~Rs 172.6 cr microfinance interest wrongly booked as fee income; CEO Sumant Kathpalia and deputy CEO resigned (Apr-2025); first quarterly loss in ~two decades (Q4FY25, ~Rs 2,328 cr); SEBI's ex-parte interim order (28-May-2025) barred the two ex-executives for alleged insider trading -- findings against executives, not the promoter; IIHL said it remained committed to support. Earlier, the 2018-19 IL&FS-linked and loan-quality divergences at IndusInd drew RBI scrutiny. HGS: how the ~Rs 8,000 cr healthcare-BPO sale proceeds (2021) were deployed (NXTDIGITAL merger, treasury) drew minority questions (unverified detail). Ashok Leyland is professionally run with no promoter pledging. Status Nov-2026: promoter control intact; watch IIHL leverage for Reliance Capital and any family realignment after Gopichand's death.

- **regulator findings:** SEBI interim order 2025 vs IndusInd ex-CEO/deputy (insider trading)
- **red flags:** IndusInd accounting lapse 2025; family litigation; offshore promoter vehicle leverage

| # | Layer | Question it answers | Time share | Stop when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | **Map**: business model, segments, history, peers | What is the unit, and who else runs the same unit? | 5% | You can draw the value chain and name 2–3 peers with comparable units |
| L2 | **Reported financials, re-derived** | Do the numbers add up after accounting adjustments? | 15% | 10-year P&L, BS and CF re-derived; leases, goodwill, ESOP, one-offs separated |
| L3 | **Unit economics** | What does one unit earn, cost and return? | 20% | Revenue per unit and per sq ft or capacity; unit P&L; capex per unit; payback, triangulated two ways |
| L4 | **Line-by-line cost drivers in physical terms** | What *physically* drives each cost, and what is the elasticity to an external input? | 20% | **First rank cost lines by weight** (v1.1). Each line ≥3% of sales mapped to quantity × price, with a sensitivity in bps. Do security-guard depth on the top 3 lines, not on habit (wages were 3.8% of sales at VMM; minimum-wage labour was 0.3% at Cummins, where materials were 63%) |
| L5 | **Governance, ownership, incentives, related parties** | Who gets paid before minority shareholders? | 10% (**15% for MNC subsidiaries/group companies**, taken from L3) | RPT table by year and share of each cost line; promoter/PE supply; KMP incentives and strike prices; **for MNC subs, the parent-take table** (see below) |
| L6 | **Customer, competitor, supplier ground truth** | Does reality match the disclosures? | 20% | Scuttlebutt list executed or scheduled; each observation tied to a model number |
| L7 | **Flag override and synthesis** | Which numbers mislead, in either direction? | 10% | Override table filled; open-flag count; "what would change my mind" per flag |

For a 1-day screen, do L1–L2 plus the L4 top-3 costs plus the L5 RPT table only. **L5's RPT table is never skipped.**

**L2 additions (v1.1), always:**
- **Customer concentration** from the Ind AS 108 footnote ("sales of ₹X derived from N external customers", each ≥10% of revenue). Track N and the share by year. At Cummins it went from 2 customers/21% to 3 customers/31%.
- **Other-income decomposition:** treasury interest, MF gains, group rent, JV/associate dividends. Compute **core PBT = PBT − other income** and use it for multiples. At Cummins, other income was 23% of PBT.
- Screener nets exceptional items into "Other income". Read the AR P&L.

Screener cross-check: borrowings 3,957 (Mar-25) -> 5,378 (Mar-26) -> 6,305 (Sep-26); FY26 CFO -INR 414 cr, FCF -691 cr; debtor days 84 -> 101; working-capital days 42 -> 57.
- **Segments:** Civil "+15%" (Feb-25), then "at least +25%" (May-25), then "~INR 5,000 cr" (Nov-25) -> actual INR 3,823 cr (-15%). Railways "won't go below ~2,100" -> 1,555. Water INR 1,200-1,500 cr -> ~800. Non-T&D "significant uptick in Q3-Q4" -> non-T&D revenue down ~16% (derived from T&D share).
- **Dates:** E-Beam/elastomeric cables have had five dates (Q4FY26 -> Q1FY27 -> Q2FY27 -> Q2/Q3 -> Q3FY27), none acknowledged as a slip. Karnataka 500 MW: Q2 -> Q3 -> Q4FY26. Afghanistan ADB receivable: "Q3FY26" -> "Q4" -> "Q1" -> received October 2026 (three quarters late). Legacy railway projects "physically complete in 1-2 quarters" (Feb-25) were still closing in Nov-26.
- **FY27 revenue:** 12-15% (May-26, reaffirmed Aug-26 with "maybe 0.5% or 1% here and there") cut to 8-10% in Nov-26 after H1 -5.6%. Scored "withdrawn" (explicit, explained, two quarters before the deadline).
- **Governance item (single-source):** in Jul-25 an analyst asked about "this bribery case with Power Grid officials, which is under inquiry". The CEO said a PGCIL action would not hurt "our T&D growth in any manner". T&D revenue did grow (+24% in FY26), but KEC then received no PGCIL orders for ~15 months ("after a break of 15 months", Nov-26) and India T&D order intake fell to ~INR 6,400 cr (derived) from ~7,200. Scored "partly". Worth a separate check (court/CBI records) before any use.
